<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <meta name="color-scheme" content="light">
  <title>Black circle</title>
  <style>
    *, *::before, *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }
    body {
      min-height: 100vh;
      min-height: 100dvh;
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      background: #fff;
    }
    svg {
      display: block;
      width: min(400px, 90vmin);
      height: auto;
      overflow: visible;
    }
    @media (forced-colors: active) {
      circle { fill: CanvasText; }
    }
  </style>
  <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 2 2'%3E%3Ccircle cx='1' cy='1' r='1'/%3E%3C/svg%3E">
</head>
<body>
  <main>
    <svg width="400" height="400" viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="circle-title">
      <title id="circle-title">Black circle</title>
      <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="200" fill="#000"/>
    </svg>
  </main>
</body>
</html>

content.text:
I made no changes to `0.html` because I couldn't find anything clearly wrong with it. It's a black circle centred on a white page, and it already covers the usual problems:

- **Layout:** the page centres the circle with a grid and uses `100dvh`, so mobile browser toolbars don't throw off the centring.
- **Sizing:** the circle scales with `min(400px, 90vmin)` and keeps its 400×400 size if CSS doesn't load. `overflow: visible` stops the circle's edges from being cut off.
- **Accessibility:** the SVG has `role="img"` and a title, and it switches to the system text colour in high-contrast mode (`forced-colors`).
- **Other:** it has a matching favicon and states `color-scheme: light` on purpose.

Any change from here depends on what you want, so tell me which of these you mean:

1. **Dark mode:** show a white circle on a black background when the system is set to dark.
2. **Smaller file:** strip the markup down to the minimum.
3. **Visual changes:** such as a gradient, shadow or animation.
4. **Something else:** for example, a different default size or different page title/label text.
